findings.claim: NAR Article 12 and Standard of Practice 12-5 require members to present a true picture and to disclose when a listing photograph has been digitally altered.
findings.sourceTitle: NAR Code of Ethics, Article 12 and SoP 12-5

findings.claim: Disclosure is generally satisfied by a watermark on the image itself or a notation in the photo caption, with many boards preferring text legible at thumbnail size.
Virtual staging is expected to help a buyer visualise furniture placement, not to remove defects, alter dimensions or change the property's actual condition.
findings.sourceTitle: MLS Photo Requirements and Virtual Staging Disclosure Guide

findings.claim: California AB 723, reported effective 1 January 2026, is said to require a conspicuous statement on or adjacent to a digitally altered listing image plus a link or QR code to the unaltered original.
findings.caution: Sourced only from competitor marketing pages. Do NOT state this as fact in a post without a primary legislative citation.

findings.claim: Reported penalties for undisclosed virtual staging range from board fines to listing removal and complaints to the state real estate board.
findings.sourceTitle: MLS Virtual Staging Rules and Disclosure Requirements
findings.caution: Specific dollar ranges vary by source and are not board-verified. Do not quote a figure.
